Hi Karthik,

Thanks for your earlier demo — the product looked promising. As part of our vendor evaluation we need a clear written response on support and customer success coverage. The RFx we received asks for specifics in these areas: assigned TAM model, support hours for different severity levels, on-call/engineering escalation flow, incident communications cadence/templates, and any SLAs for response/resolution. Also note we will need evidence of any SOC2 or audit artifacts related to incident handling.

Can you provide:
- A short summary of TAM coverage options for enterprise (what's included vs add-on)
- Typical SLA commitments for P1-P4 incidents and escalation path (who we contact at each step)
- How incident comms to customer stakeholders are handled (template or cadence)
- Contact & escalation examples for cross-region outages (APAC vs US)
- Attach any supporting docs (TAM matrix, incident comms template, SOC2 summary)

Goal: get this by EOD Thursday so our sourcing team can include in the consolidated RFP response.

Karthik / team —

Draft below for Orion. I kept it tight and operational — easy to drop into their RFP template. Please review for accuracy and any legal/PII concerns.

1) TAM coverage options (enterprise):
- Standard TAM (included): 9x5 account coverage, weekly office hours, onboarding support, quarterly business reviews, access to shared Slack channel for priority queue.
- Premier TAM (add-on): 24x7 escalation coverage, dedicated on-call TAM, weekly operational reviews, quarterly architecture deep dives, prioritized capacity and rollback coordination.
- TAM assignments are scoped by committed spend and reserved capacity. For enterprise deals we typically recommend Premier for production SLAs.

2) Support hours & SLA targets (typical):
- P1 (service down / critical customer impact): Initial response within 1 hour; 24x7 remediation coordination until resolved (Premier) or active during business hours with on-call escalation (Standard).
- P2 (major degradation): Initial response within 4 hours; engaged engineering support based on severity; target remediation 8-48 hours depending on root cause.
- P3 (partial impact / feature bug): Initial response within 24 hours; fix/mitigation planned in next release cycle or hotfix if priority.
- P4 (informational / enhancement): Initial acknowledgement within 3 business days; scheduled per product roadmap.

3) Escalation path (example):
- Tier 1: Redwood Support Portal / Email (support@redwood.com) -> triage & known-issue checks.
- Tier 2: Assigned TAM (for enterprise) -> deeper ops troubleshooting, runbook activation.
- Tier 3: On-call Engineering / Platform SRE -> kernel/runtime investigation, hotfix coordination.
- Executive: Customer success director -> leadership-level updates, credits, and contractual remedies.

4) Incident communications & cadence (we provide templates):
- Major incident (P1) cadence: 0h acknowledgement, 1h initial incident summary, 4h engineering update, hourly updates until mitigation, post-incident report within 72 hours.
- Stakeholder channels: dedicated Slack channel (or bridging if customer prefers), email distribution list, and incident page on status.redwood.com.
- We provide a customizable Incident_Communication_Template.docx that includes stakeholder mapping, suggested subject lines, and update cadence.

5) Cross-region handling & contacts:
- For APAC incidents we align to local on-call rotations; TAM will coordinate with regional SREs and provide localized update windows where possible.
- Primary escalation contacts: support@redwood.com (portal), customer TAM (name/contact included when assigned), on-call eng via PagerDuty.

6) Evidence & artifacts: SOC2 Type II summary available on request (we provide an executive summary and scope; full report under NDA). We can also provide recent incident postmortems (redacted) on request.

Attachments planned: Redwood_TAM_Matrix.pdf (coverage by tier), Incident_Communication_Template.docx, Redwood_Support_SLA_v3.pdf.

If everyone signs off I will assemble and Karthik can send to Lisa.

— Grace
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the clear list. Please find our formal responses below and a short set of attachments. I've highlighted the items that typically require contract language or an add-on.

Summary (attached docs): Redwood_TAM_Matrix.pdf, Redwood_Support_SLA_v3.pdf, Incident_Communication_Template.docx, Redwood_TAM_Coverage_Table.xlsx, SOC2_Summary_redacted.pdf (available under NDA).

Key points:
- TAM: Standard TAM (included) = 9x5 account coverage; Premier TAM (add-on) = dedicated 24x7 coverage with on-call TAM and prioritized capacity coordination. (See TAM matrix.)
- SLAs: P1 initial response = 1 hour; P2 = 4 hours; P3 = 24 hours; P4 = 3 business days. Formal SLA credits and uptime targets are part of our Dedicated/Reserved capacity contracts.
- Escalation path: support@redwood.com -> Assigned TAM -> On-call Engineering (PagerDuty) -> CS Director / Exec escalation. We will provide named contacts once the SOW is executed.
- Incident comms: We follow the cadence Grace outlined. For P1 incidents we provide hourly engineering updates and a post-incident report within 72 hours. We can run regular tabletop exercises with your ops team during onboarding.
- Cross-region: Our regional SRE rotations cover APAC/EU/US; TAM coordinates regional notifications and localized customer windows.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm if Premier TAM is required for your production rollout (recommended).
2) If you want the SOC2 summary, we need an NDA — I can share the redacted summary immediately once proc confirms.
3) We can schedule a 30–45 minute walkthrough w/ Grace + LA dev on Friday to go through the incident comms template and runbook (suggested).

Karthik —

Thanks for the detailed write-up and attachments. A couple quick clarifications before we fold this into the RFP:

1) For P1 incidents under Standard TAM, you say "on-call escalation (Standard)" — can you confirm whether Standard customers get 24x7 on-call engineering for P1, or is 24x7 remediation only for Premier? We need to be specific in the RFP.
2) For the incident postmortem window (72 hours) — does that include a root cause analysis with remediation plan and timeline, or is it an initial post-incident summary with a later RCA?
3) Please include the default channels (email, Slack, PagerDuty) and confirm who will be the first phone escalation number for P1 (we prefer a direct on-call phone bridge).

Procurement also asked whether TAM assignment is guaranteed within contract signature or only after a usage threshold is hit.

Appreciate the help — Lisa

Subject: Re: Question set: TAM coverage / escalation processes (RFP)

Hi Lisa —

Great questions, answered inline below to make it easy to paste into the RFP: 

1) 24x7 on-call engineering:
- Standard TAM: Initial response SLA for P1 incidents is 1 hour during Redwood business hours (9x5). We maintain an on-call engineering rotation for critical issues; however, 24x7 active remediation coordination (continuous engineering presence and bridge ownership) is only guaranteed under Premier TAM. For the RFP we recommend specifying Premier for guaranteed 24x7 remediation.

2) Post-incident report / RCA timing: 
- Our 72-hour post-incident report is an initial RCA draft that includes the incident timeline, immediate mitigations, and planned remediation steps. A final, detailed RCA with full remediation timeline is typically delivered within 10 business days for complex outages.

3) Escalation channels and primary phone bridge: 
- Channels: support@redwood.com (portal + email), dedicated Slack channel (optional), PagerDuty for on-call eng alerts.
- Primary phone escalation: Premier TAM customers receive a dedicated on-call phone bridge number and direct dial to the TAM/on-call engineer. For Standard customers we provide escalation to on-call eng via PagerDuty and the support portal; direct phone bridge is provided as part of Premier.

4) TAM assignment timing: 
- TAMs are assigned at contract signature for Premier TAM and for enterprise deals with reserved capacity. For Standard TAM (included) we assign a shared TAM during onboarding; a named TAM is typically confirmed once minimum usage thresholds or reserved capacity commitments are met. We can include guaranteed named-TAM language as part of the SOW if required.

If you'd like, Grace and I can join procurement's call this afternoon to read this into the RFP.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
